name: The path in the Abhidharmakośa (Sarvāstivāda-Vaibhāṣika)

stages.name: vṛttastha
stages.description: Keeping the prātimokṣa discipline.

stages.name: śruta-cintā
stages.description: Wisdom born of hearing and of reflection, with name and meaning as object.

stages.name: kāya-citta-viveka, āryavaṃśa
stages.description: Contentment and few desires; the four noble lineages.

stages.name: avatāra: aśubhā / ānāpānasmṛti
stages.description: Calm (śamatha) through the two gateways, by temperament.

stages.name: smṛtyupasthāna
stages.description: Examining body, feeling, mind, dharmas by particular then general characteristics.

stages.name: ūṣmagata
stages.description: First root of penetration: the four truths in sixteen aspects.

stages.name: mūrdhan
stages.description: One never again cuts the roots of good.

stages.name: kṣānti
stages.description: One no longer goes to bad destinies.

stages.name: laukikāgradharma
stages.description: One moment, immediately before the path of seeing.

stages.name: darśanamārga
stages.description: Fifteen moments of acceptance and knowledge of the four truths.

stages.name: bhāvanāmārga
stages.description: From the sixteenth moment; abandoning the defilements of the nine planes grade by grade through the fruits.

stages.name: vajropama-samādhi
stages.description: The last uninterrupted path, destroying the last defilement.

stages.name: aśaikṣamārga / kṣayajñāna
stages.description: Knowledge of destruction (and of non-arising for the unshakeable).

notes: Later scholastic tradition (Chinese: 'three wise and four good roots'; Tibetan: the five paths) groups stages 1–5 as the accumulation/preparation phases. Bands are the interpretation layer (see interpretation_log).

name: The four candidates and four fruits (Abhidharmakośa)

stages.name: srotaāpatti-phala-pratipannaka
stages.description: Follower through faith / through dharma during the fifteen moments.

stages.name: srotaāpanna
stages.description: From the sixteenth moment; 'seven times at most' or 'family to family'.

stages.name: sakṛdāgāmi-pratipannaka
stages.description: Abandoning the first five grades of desire-realm defilement.

stages.name: sakṛdāgāmin
stages.description: Six grades abandoned.

stages.name: anāgāmi-pratipannaka
stages.description: Seven or eight grades abandoned ('one interval').

stages.name: anāgāmin
stages.description: Nine grades abandoned; many kinds (in the intermediate state, on arising, upward-going …); with cessation, a body-witness.

stages.name: arhattva-pratipannaka
stages.description: Abandoning the defilements of the upper realms up to the eighth grade of the peak of existence.

stages.name: arhat
stages.description: Knowledge of destruction; six kinds.

stages.name: first incalculable aeon
stages.gloss: from the vow before the former Śākyamuni to Ratnaśikhin
stages.description: Beginning of the career (the tradition: first vow under a Buddha Śākyamuni of the past).

stages.name: second incalculable aeon
stages.description: Ending with the Buddha Dīpaṅkara.

stages.name: third incalculable aeon
stages.description: Ending with the Buddha Vipaśyin.

stages.name: one hundred aeons
stages.description: From now he is 'a bodhisattva' in the strict sense: always in good destinies, male, remembering births, not turning back.

stages.name: fulfilment of the perfections
stages.gloss: giving, patience, morality, vigour, meditation, wisdom
stages.description: Meditation and wisdom are fulfilled immediately before awakening.

stages.name: awakening in thirty-four moments
stages.gloss: sixteen of seeing, eighteen of cultivation (bhāṣya)
stages.description: Attaining the attainment of cessation together with awakening.

stages.name: turning the wheel of Dharma
stages.description: All Buddhas are equal in acting for the good of the world.

name: The ten grounds of the bodhisattva (Mahāvastu)

stages.name: durārohā
stages.description: The first ground; the text details the conduct and the qualities that lead to it.

stages.name: durjayā
stages.description: From the seventh ground the bodhisattva does not turn back (low confidence).

stages.name: abhiṣeka
stages.description: The tenth ground (abhiṣekavatī) ends at Mvu i.193.

notes: Names checked in the local e-text (Mvu i.76); page ranges from the colophons ending each bhūmi in the e-text; contents of each ground not summarized here. Bands are tentative.

name: The four conducts of the bodhisattva (Mahāvastu)

stages.name: prakṛticaryā
stages.description: Planting roots of merit before a Buddha (under Aparājitadhvaja).

stages.name: praṇidhānacaryā
stages.description: The first vow to become a Buddha (under a former Śākyamuni).

stages.name: anulomacaryā
stages.description: Conduct in accordance with the vow (under Samitāvin).

stages.name: anivartanacaryā
stages.description: After Dīpaṅkara's prediction.
